lists.AI Context Optimization: AI Context Optimization covers tools that compress, select, rerank, or compact context for LLM agents, often using Jev/TypeSafe AI to fit token budgets. It is not general Typesafe-Jev, Agent Memory, or RAG/GraphRAG; those lack the focus on on-the-fly context reduction.
lists.AI Design Tools: Contains AI-powered tools for design tasks like graphics, product, or UI design. Confused with UI Design Tools (non-AI), Automation (AI Powered), and Business Tools (AI); excludes non-AI design tools and general AI automation or business tools.
lists.Agent Harness: Repositories providing execution runtimes, orchestration, or decision-to-action harnesses for autonomous AI agents, especially coding agents, that manage agent processes, approvals, and actions. Excludes Agent Skills, Agent Tool-call, Agent Memory, Inference Engines, and LLM Models; those cover specific agent capabilities or underlying models, not the harness itself.
lists.Agent Memory: AI agent memory systems: session persistence, fact invalidation, and memory lifecycle management. Not for Agent Skills, Agent Tool-call, AI Context Optimization, or Typesafe-Jev; excludes general agent harnesses and RAG/GraphRAG.
lists.Agent Skills: Repositories providing installable skills, commands, rules, and hooks that extend AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Confused with Agent Harness or Agent Tool-call; harnesses, tool-call infrastructure, model routing, and general automation do not belong.
lists.Agent Tool-call: Repos for executing, routing, guarding, and connecting AI agent tool calls (MCP gateways, OpenRouter-style routers, runtime constraint checks), typically TypeScript. Confused with Agent Skills, Agent Harness, and Typesafe-Jev; excludes skill definitions, agent harnesses, and general automation.
lists.Automation (AI Powered): Repositories here use AI (often Jev/TypeSafe) to automate tasks like browser interaction, testing, document classification, and commit analysis. Do not confuse with Automation (Non-ai first), which lacks AI, or Typesafe-Jev, which focuses on the model itself rather than automation applications.
lists.Automation (Non-ai first): Non-AI tooling that automates developer and desktop workflows, like CI/CD pipeline modules and native launcher, hotkey, or clipboard utilities. Distinct from Automation (AI Powered) and Business Tools (Non-AI), which cover AI-driven or business-specific tasks rather than general scripting and system automation.
lists.Awesome Lists: Curated "awesome" lists and catalogs, especially those indexing open-source projects built with Jev or TypeSafe Jev. Not lists about Jev models or alternatives themselves, which belong in Typesafe-Jev or Jev Model Alternatives.
lists.Backend Scaling: Repositories focused on scaling backend services, including load balancing, horizontal scaling, caching, and traffic performance. Likely confused with Frameworks/libraries, Database tools, and Agent Harness; general web frameworks, individual databases, and AI agent tooling do not belong here.
lists.Business Tools (AI): AI-powered business tools, like usenotra/notra, that turn work into content. Confused with Business Tools (Non-AI); non-AI business tools and generic AI automation belong elsewhere.
lists.Business Tools (Non-AI): This List is for non-AI business tools. It is most likely confused with Business Tools (AI), which takes AI-powered business tools, and Automation (Non-ai first); AI agents, LLM tools, and generic automation do not belong here.
lists.Database tools: PostgreSQL extensions and tools integrating Jev/TypeSafe for semantic or categorical querying, like pg_typesafe, pg-jev, and jevql. Not general database utilities; distinct from Typesafe-Jev (broader Jev projects), SQLite (different engine), and Frameworks/libraries.
lists.Frameworks/libraries: Reusable packages and plugins developers import or install — Python libraries, pytest plugins, dataframe toolkits, CLIs, and runtimes like Univer — rather than the Jev modelling method itself. Distinct from Typesafe-Jev and Jev Model Alternatives, which cover the underlying semantic/probability approach, not shipped frameworks and libraries.
lists.Inference Engines: This List contains runtime inference engines that execute LLM or structured decision workloads, such as TokenSpeed and DeepOpen. It is not for LLM models (LLM Models) or local LLM tools (Local LLM tools), but for the engines themselves.
lists.Jev Model Alternatives: Open-source alternatives to Jev/TypeSafe Jev: calibrated, non-autoregressive System One decision engines. Not the original Typesafe-Jev list, nor general Small Language Models or Inference Engines.
lists.LLM Model Routing: Repositories for routing LLM requests to the best model or checkpoint, often using classifiers or non-autoregressive decision engines (e.g., TypeSafe Jev). Not general LLM models or inference engines; distinct from Typesafe-Jev and Jev Model Alternatives, which focus on the Jev engine itself.
lists.LLM Models: Repositories presenting or implementing large language models themselves, such as Contrastive-LM/CLM and ZDTaichu5.0-9B, typically Python model code or releases. Not for inference engines, routing, local LLM tools, or small language models; those belong in Inference Engines, LLM Model Routing, Local LLM tools, and Small Language Models respectively.
lists.Local LLM tools: Tools for running or demoing LLMs locally, like llama.cpp-, MLX-, or small-model-based runners and wrappers. Not hosted LLM APIs, model weights, or inference engines themselves, which belong in Inference Engines or LLM Models.
lists.Other: This List holds repositories that do not fit any named sibling List. It is most likely confused with Awesome Lists, Frameworks/libraries, and Business Tools (Non-AI); anything clearly matching those specific themes belongs there, not here.
lists.Programming Languages: This List covers programming languages themselves—compilers, runtimes, and language implementations like Bend. It differs from Frameworks/libraries, which holds general software libraries, and from Jev-related Lists (Typesafe-Jev, Jev Model Alternatives) that concern one specific language rather than languages generally.
lists.RAG/GraphRAG: RAG/GraphRAG lists repositories for retrieval-augmented generation: semantic code/text search, reranking, and RAG pipelines, as seen in Jev-powered nlgrep and reranker. Most likely confused with Typesafe-Jev, Agent Memory, or AI Context Optimization; exclude generic agent skills, model routing, and inference engines.
lists.SQLite: Projects that add natural-language, Jev-powered predicates to SQLite—batch/cached/cost-guarded filtering, ranking, or classification—belong here. Not general SQLite drivers, database tools, or standalone TypeSafe-Jev work; those fit Database tools or Typesafe-Jev.
lists.Small Language Models: Small, non-LLM language models and proof-of-concept byte-level or recurrent models built with MLX belong here. Do not confuse with LLM Models, Local LLM tools, or Inference Engines, which cover full-scale LLMs and serving tools, not small experimental models.
lists.Typesafe-Jev: Repositories that build on, integrate, or provide examples for TypeSafe's Jev decision model, across TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Elixir. Excludes Jev alternatives (Jev Model Alternatives) and general agent skills (Agent Skills) not using Jev.
lists.UI Design Tools: Reserved for repositories about user-interface design tooling rather than UI code frameworks. Most likely confused with UI Frameworks and AI Design Tools; implementation libraries and AI-only design generators do not belong.
lists.UI Frameworks: For code libraries and frameworks used to build user interfaces, such as component and rendering tooling. Most confused with Frameworks/libraries and UI Design Tools; generic backend or non-UI libraries, visual design tools, and AI design tools do not belong.
lists.Wordpress: Repositories specific to the CMS named in the title, such as its plugins, themes, and site tooling, belong here. Do not add general web frameworks/libraries or backend-scaling projects; those belong in Frameworks/libraries or Backend Scaling.
